explanation: Hydrogen and helium are alone in the top row because the innermost electron shell holds just two electrons. The second row then holds eight elements, from lithium to neon.

claims.text: The first row (period 1) of the periodic table holds two elements, hydrogen and helium.
The first row of the periodic table does not hold 8, 10 or 18 elements; 8 is the count of the second and third rows, and 18 of the fourth and fifth.
The innermost electron shell of an atom holds at most two electrons.
The second row (period 2) of the periodic table holds eight elements, from lithium (atomic number 3) to neon (atomic number 10).
